details.bidirectionality: Forward direction causal; block equals explicit forward-plus-reversed scan and first position depends on last.
details.mamba_equivalence: Outputs, input gradients, and all parameter gradients match sequential recurrence.
details.target_leakage: Forward accepts prefix and output length only; observed embedded suffix consists solely of MASK. Each block called once.

scope: Tiny CPU unit tests, no performance benchmarking, no live service access. Dense FP32 tiny architecture ablation, not routed/quantized AGILLM or 600B validation.
review_findings: Mamba-1 selective recurrence with input-dependent delta/B/C, diagonal negative A, causal depthwise convolution, D skip, SiLU gate. Bidirectionality is an explicit independent-two-direction extension.
Fixed-step same-seed training uses deterministic identical NumPy data batches; verify stored hashes after fits. LR selection occurs on validation, test data first evaluated after final fits.
5 s snapshots are first whole step crossing budget, not strict identical elapsed times. Compare recorded elapsed and steps; training timing excludes data preparation, validation, checkpoint saving.

Attention uses optimized PyTorch SDPA while Mamba uses unfused O(T log T) work associative scan with repeated allocations. Timing is implementation-specific CPU performance, not asymptotic or CUDA comparison.
PAD embeddings participate in attention/scan for toy prompts. Same inputs for both models, no padding mask; not a leakage channel.

Text exact48 screening covers only actual 2 MB training prefix and within-evaluation duplicates; shorter/natural phrase overlap and same-source correlation remain. Byte suffix loss measures factorized conditional prediction, not autoregressive perplexity or general intelligence.
Three seeds and tiny training budget limit uncertainty claims; test-example resampling alone must not imply training-seed uncertainty.
NAT kind values other than transformer silently select Mamba; current explicit call sites use valid strings. out_len=0 unsupported by slicing; fixed protocol uses 16.
